page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-128GB is a memory-oriented virtual machine deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 16 x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz with one thread per core. The instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. CPU vector capabilities include AVX, AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), and AVX-VNNI extensions alongside cryptographic hardware acceleration including AES and SHA-NI. The server includes no bundled local storage, no integrated GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote block storage and external routing configurations.

Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng tests alongside solid mid-tier multi-core execution. Geekbench metrics yield 1913.0 for single-core and 11996.0 for multi-core processing, while Clang compilation and ray tracing tests operate squarely in the middle 50 percent range. Memory subsystems sustain 152.59 GB/sec read and 73.41 GB/sec write throughput on large 256 MB blocks, although synthetic PassMark memory evaluations register in the bottom quartile. Key-value caching performance reaches 24.21 million Redis SET operations per second, with static web serving throughput hitting 32.47 GB/sec. Low-overhead workloads scale well, though single-threaded bzip3 decompression and 7B parameter LLM text generation demonstrate weaker relative efficiency.

Because compute cycles rely on a shared CPU allocation model, this instance provides a cost-effective hardware profile for memory-demanding applications that do not require dedicated core isolation. The substantial 128 GB memory footprint makes it suitable for in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, intermediate ETL processing pipelines, memory-heavy testing clusters, and staging environments where memory capacity outweighs raw continuous CPU execution.
